newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end up, Hang Seng at 31-month high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end up, Hang Seng at 31-month high.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended firmer on Tuesday and the Hang Seng index hit its highest close since February 1994, buoyed by Wall Street's highs and the view that a near-term rate hike would not hit stocks hard, brokers said.

"With precious little news on the domestic front, Hong Kong remains tied to the U.S. interest rate outlook -- which now looks limited to a 0.25 percent hike," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
The Hang Seng Index closed up 53.71 points, 0.46 percent, at 11,621.61, off a peak of 11,645.35. The blue-chip barometer last closed higher at 12,157.57 on February 4, 1994.
